title: Research
text:
My research interests center on computational statistics and scientific computing, particularly where machine learning and mathematical modeling can reveal structure in complex data.


Directed Networks and Resting-State Effective Brain Connectivity with State-Space Reconstruction Using Reservoir Computing Causality
Joan Falcó-Roget, Adrian Onicas, Felix Akwasi-Sarpong, Alessandro Crimi (2023).
This work studies effective connectivity in resting-state brain networks using reservoir-computing causality and state-space reconstruction. It connects time-series modeling, nonlinear dynamics, machine learning, and computational neuroscience.
Open DOI





I am interested in methods that balance prediction, interpretability, and computational efficiency, including regularization and high-dimensional models.



My computational work includes numerical optimization, iterative algorithms, simulation, and matrix-based methods for scientific problems.



I have worked with longitudinal and survival-analysis methods and am interested in rigorous statistical approaches to biomedical and population-health questions.



I use R, Python, Quarto, LaTeX, and Git to create workflows in which the analysis, figures, code, and final report can be reproduced from a transparent source.

title: Projects
text:
STAT 8672 · Georgia State University · Spring 2026
Built a large-scale predictive modeling workflow using NYC TLC Yellow Taxi data. Compared ridge, lasso, and elastic-net models with glmnet, emphasizing regularization, validation, and scalable statistical learning.
Tools: R · glmnet · data preprocessing · model validation



STAT 8540 · Georgia State University · Spring 2026
Analyzed normalized whole-brain volume in the OASIS cohort using longitudinal response-profile methods, with attention to repeated measurements and appropriate covariance modeling.
Tools: R · longitudinal models · GLS · statistical inference



Implemented simulation-based Bayesian analyses using Monte Carlo and Gibbs-sampling methods, with reproducible R workflows and posterior summaries.
Tools: R · Bayesian inference · Monte Carlo · Gibbs sampling



Implemented and studied optimization methods including golden-section search, steepest descent, conjugate-gradient methods, Newton/Levenberg-Marquardt ideas, and constrained optimization.
Tools: R/Python · numerical methods · optimization



Graduate research exploring causality detection in time-series data using machine-learning approaches, contributing to later work on reservoir-computing causality and brain connectivity.
Tools: Python · machine learning · time series · reservoir computing

title: About
text: I am Felix Akwasi Sarpong, a Ghanaian mathematician and statistician pursuing graduate study at Georgia State University in Atlanta. My academic path has moved from mathematics and statistics into scientific computing, machine learning, optimization, and computational research.

title: About
text:
Academic path
My training includes undergraduate study at Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology (KNUST), graduate mathematical-sciences training at AIMS Ghana, and graduate work in the Department of Mathematics and Statistics at Georgia State University.
At AIMS Ghana, my research included machine learning for time-series causality. That work contributed to research on resting-state effective brain connectivity using reservoir computing, connecting mathematical modeling, machine learning, and computational neuroscience.
At Georgia State, my graduate work has included statistical learning, Bayesian data analysis, survival analysis, computational optimization, biostatistics, experimental design, and pattern recognition.
